title: Health-management algorithm racial-bias study
system_purpose: Identify patients for high-risk care-management support
affected_groups: Black patients; White patients; care-management teams
verified_facts: The peer-reviewed study found that an algorithm using health-care cost as a proxy for health needs produced racial bias at a given risk score.
reported_harm: Black patients were less likely to receive additional help despite being sicker at the same score; the harm is inequitable allocation of care-management resources.
quantitative_evidence: The study estimated changing the target would increase Black patients receiving additional help from 17.7% to 46.5%.
limitations: The publication does not evaluate a chat interface, Vietnam population, or a symptom-routing model.

title: External validation of Epic Sepsis Model
system_purpose: Predict sepsis risk for inpatient clinical workflow
decision_impact: Clinical alerting and potential timing of antibiotic response
verified_facts: The external-validation study evaluated a proprietary model implemented at hundreds of hospitals and reported missed timely-antibiotic cases among patients with sepsis.
reported_harm: Missed or poorly calibrated alerts can contribute to delayed recognition, while excessive or unhelpful alerts can burden clinicians; the study does not prove causation for each outcome.
quantitative_evidence: The study states the model identified 183 of 2,552 patients with sepsis who did not receive timely antibiotics.
limitations: The evaluation is an inpatient predictive model at a study setting, not a causal study of treatment outcomes or a consumer triage chatbot.

title: NEDA Tessa eating-disorder chatbot suspension
system_purpose: Provide information and support related to eating disorders
affected_groups: People seeking eating-disorder support; advocates; care providers
verified_facts: NPR reported that NEDA took down Tessa after the chatbot provided weight-loss advice outside the intended program.
reported_harm: Users and advocates reported that weight-loss guidance could harm people with eating disorders; the product was removed rather than continuing as support.
quantitative_evidence: The report does not provide a reliable denominator or rate of harmful conversations.
limitations: Reporting notes disputed explanations for the failure; evidence is not a controlled assessment of clinical safety or of all health chatbots.
